title: Gougères
notes: Keeps warm in an 80 °C oven for up to 45 min.
Freezes 1 month fully baked; recrisp 6 min at 180 °C from frozen.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, no fan, with racks in the upper and lower thirds.
Put {water}, {milk}, {butter}, {salt}, {nutmeg} and {pepper} in the TM7 bowl. Heat until fully melted and just bubbling. TM7: 5 min / 98 °C / speed 1
Mix in {flour} until combined. TM7: 20 sec / speed 4
Cook until the dough forms a smooth ball pulling from the sides and leaves a thin film on the bowl. TM7: 3 min / 100 °C / speed 3
Mix without heat to bring the dough below about 60 °C, so the eggs will not scramble. TM7: 1 min / speed 3
Add {egg} in 3 additions, mixing after each, keeping back the last few spoonfuls. TM7: 1 min 30 sec / speed 4

Lift the spatula: the dough should stretch into a V-shaped ribbon that slowly breaks, glossy and holding soft ridges like thick mayonnaise. If it snaps stiffly, add the reserved egg a spoonful at a time, mixing briefly after each.
Add {gruyere} and {parmesan}. Mix just to distribute, without overworking. TM7: 15 sec / speed 3.5
Spoon 4 cm mounds onto two trays lined with baking paper, 4 cm apart. Smooth the points with a finger dipped in water so they do not burn.
Optional: sprinkle a little flaky salt on each.
Bake on the two racks. Do not open the door.
Turn the oven down to 185 °C, still without opening the door.
Open the door for 2 seconds to let the steam out, then bake until deep golden.
Take the trays out and pierce each puff on the side with a skewer.
Turn the oven off and return the trays, door ajar, to dry.
Bring to the table while still warm.
